text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Senior Chinese Politburo member and Chairman of the National People's Congress Qiao Shi met Vietnam's Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and his Vietnamese counterpart, National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh. Qiao and Kiet agreed to solve all remaining problems between the two countries by negotiations based on equality and friendship.
-- The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is to grant the Vietnamese government $24 million to help it achieve its population and development objectives between 1997 and 2000.

-- Export revenues from coffee are falling due to falling prices on the world market. Exports jumped to 231,000 tonnes for the 1995-96 crop, but the $420 million earned was a 25-percent fall compared with the previous year.
-- Politburo member Lieutenant-General Le Kha Phieu has called on the official Vietnam News Agency to provide timely and accurate information.
-- Five people were killed and hundreds of houses were totally destroyed in flash flooding after torrential rain in the central coastal province of Binh Dinh last week.

-- South Korean President Kim Young-sam told the chairman of Vietnam Journalist Association Phan Quang that Vietnam should continue improving its investment environment and adjusting the economic structure further to attract more South Korean investors.
-- Vietnam exported 420,000 tonnes of rice in October.
